style.visual_cues: Use clear glass boundaries, plausible refraction, edge highlights, and limited dispersion with a recognizable background visible through the form. Animate droplets, lenses, or flexible panels while maintaining continuity between deformation and refraction. Ordinary translucent blur does not provide this optical treatment.
style.note: The source directly names or describes this visual direction. Explicitly named in the source; not interchangeable with frosted glass.

recommended_stack.name: HyperFrames
recommended_stack.runtime: HTML composition in browser; CLI orchestration in Node.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Primary pipeline for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. Visual construction and motion design remain owned by the selected style renderer and motion engine.

suggested_libraries.name: GSAP
suggested_libraries.purpose: Build a paused, seekable timeline and register it with HyperFrames after construction is complete.

recommended_stack.style_application: Compose the output of the selected visual and motion layers. Supply seekable time or integrate baked assets; do not replace the style-specific rendering or motion method with framework defaults.
recommended_stack.selection_guidance: Use HyperFrames by default. Fall back to Remotion only when the documented fallback condition is met, and record the reason. Do not mix framework APIs.

recommended_stack.name: Three.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Build scenes, cameras, geometry, materials, and lighting. Drive animation from a shared, seekable time source.
recommended_stack.style_application: Apply this tool to Liquid Glass according to visual_cues and tech.implementation.

recommended_stack.name: MeshPhysicalMaterial
recommended_stack.purpose: Use transmission, ior, roughness, and related parameters for glass and physical surface reflections.
recommended_stack.style_application: Apply this tool to Liquid Glass according to visual_cues and tech.implementation.

recommended_stack.name: Offscreen Rendering
recommended_stack.purpose: Render the background into a texture for material or shader sampling. Avoid sampling the active render target in a feedback loop.
recommended_stack.style_application: Apply this tool to Liquid Glass according to visual_cues and tech.implementation.

recommended_stack.name: Remotion
recommended_stack.runtime: React in browser; rendering orchestrated by Node.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Conditional fallback pipeline for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. Visual construction and motion design remain owned by the selected style renderer and motion engine.
recommended_stack.style_application: Compose the output of the selected visual and motion layers. Supply seekable time or integrate baked assets; do not replace the style-specific rendering or motion method with framework defaults.
recommended_stack.selection_guidance: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.

recommended_stack.name: chroma.js
recommended_stack.purpose: Optionally validate colors, derive controlled palette variants, interpolate colors, and check foreground/background contrast.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Start with task-provided colors and the style visual_cues. Keep a shared, deterministic palette and named color tokens. Generate gradients or interpolate colors only when the style permits them; keep limited-palette, monochrome, pixel, and print treatments discrete where required. Evaluate animated color from shared composition time. Check contrast against the actual composited background; a two-color ratio alone does not verify text over transparency, gradients, textures, or video. Pass output through the selected renderer's color API and preserve its color-space handling. Native CSS/SVG colors remain sufficient when no color processing is needed.
recommended_stack.style_application: Read palette.tokens, palette.constraints and palette.agent_instruction for Liquid Glass. Validate approved colors and assess readable existing token pairs with chroma-js. Use palette.gradient only when enabled and appropriate. Preserve task/reference colors exactly; optional suggested tokens are fallback inputs, not permission to recolor assets.

tech.implementation: Use transmission and refraction materials for 3D glass, or explicitly labeled screen-space displacement for a 2D approximation. Preserve text readability and stable boundaries.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Liquid Glass without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

style.executable_prompt_template:
Replace all double-brace placeholders with task inputs before execution. Use documented defaults only for omitted optional inputs and state the assumptions.
Create a Liquid Glass video about {{subject}} for {{audience_and_objective}}. Use {{assets_and_exact_copy}}. Deliver a video of {{duration_seconds}} seconds, with aspect ratio {{aspect_ratio}}, resolution {{resolution}}, and frame rate {{frame_rate}}. Follow {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} and save deliverables to {{output_directory}}.
Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition and export only. If omitted, resolve it to tech.framework_selection.default. Check the primary framework first; use tech.framework_selection.fallback only when the documented fallback_condition is met, and record the verified reason. An existing React project alone is not sufficient reason to switch.
1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Use clear glass boundaries, plausible refraction, edge highlights, and limited dispersion with a recognizable background visible through the form. Animate droplets, lenses, or flexible panels while maintaining continuity between deformation and refraction. Ordinary translucent blur does not provide this optical treatment. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Use transmission and refraction materials for 3D glass, or explicitly labeled screen-space displacement for a 2D approximation. Preserve text readability and stable boundaries. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

motion_references.selection_policy: Optional candidates are screened for natural style compatibility. Before selection, inspect the actual scene illustration, assets, geometry and narrative beat. Keep only references whose defining action is supported by that scene. Choosing no reference is valid. Do not infer motion from a similar label; do not replace the existing style motion direction.

candidates.usage_guidance: Consider anchored cards progressively covered by incoming cards, with optional scale or dimming for recession and a defined stack release. Keep active content readable and simulate sticky or pinned behavior with time-driven layers in video.

Consider pointer-driven perspective tilt with optional separated depth layers and a neutral return. A voice or waveform is content layered onto the motion; choose playback separately and do not infer spatial audio from card depth.

Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider a horizontal card track that moves with swipe or drag and settles at a defined snap selection. Preserve readable cards, accessible navigation, and one track-position owner; author the track directly for video.

Consider a cohesive orb deformed through bounded vertex displacement or compact metaballs. Keep the form connected and time-evaluated. Energy styling, blue, and glow are optional; this visual treatment does not establish physical fluid behavior.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.
Requires real 3D depth or an explicitly labeled parallax alternative. Orbit the camera, not the subject; avoid uncontrolled full rotations.

Use a circular punctuation lens that enlarges with coherent edge highlights and refraction; never replace it with frosted blur. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

motion_references.agent_instruction: Read the actual illustration and complete pattern description, motion_sequence and video_adaptation. Identify which scene elements implement that action. Reject unsupported geometry, absent subjects, unintended depth, broken contact points or unrelated interactions. Select none when no candidate fits; use restrained style-native motion instead. Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers.

source_frame_review.sampling_limitation: One frame at each available second 01–08. No continuous motion, sub-second timing, audio or later scenes verified. Color families are visual observations; whole-frame measured dominant colors are not semantic background tokens.
source_frame_review.guidance: Choose scene-dependent backgrounds and readable coordinated colors. Separate material colors, source demonstration choices and surrounding UI/letterboxing. Existing swatches are examples, not permanent canvas restrictions. Keep explicit user-approved colors and medium-defining constraints. Only sampled seconds, not continuous motion or audio, were visually reviewed.

sources.style_evidence: Seconds 1–3 show a circular glass lens that visibly magnifies and distorts the card text beneath it, with a rim highlight and curved rim lettering. This is real refraction, not plain blur.
sources.palette_lesson:
These colours are the author's own example. Cyan-to-violet light gradients, an aqua-to-deep-teal field and then a near-black charcoal stage are scene and brand choices that move from light to dark across the acts. They are not rules of the style. The rules are these:
- Keep one cool ambient field per act behind neutral UI surfaces: white frosted, charcoal opaque or smoked translucent.
- Reserve a single saturated interactive accent (here teal) for selection, send and active states.
- Let embedded media (warm reds, photos/renders) bring the only warm colour.
- Use small semantic status colours (green waveform, orange playhead, violet active outline) sparingly on dark tiles.
For new subjects, choose the field from mood and brand. Examples: a warm coral-to-magenta for lifestyle or creator apps, a deep forest-to-moss for finance or sustainability, a graphite-to-steel-blue for developer tools, a pale mint-to-white daylight field for health, or an inky plum-to-black for a night or entertainment mood. Keep the accent hue distinct from the field and check text contrast on every translucent panel.

sources.style_evidence: The bowl's glass refracts the striped wall and red band into curved, wrapped bands (most visible at seconds 1, 2 and 8), with rim highlights and a visible boundary. The room behind stays recognizable through the glass.
sources.palette_lesson: The palette has three layers. First, the set: a room of navy/off-white stripes, a red band, a dark green wainscot and a black/white checkerboard floor, with a warm brown wooden table. Second, the medium: clear glass and a cool teal-cyan water tint. Third, the saturated accents: orange-red, yellow, blue and orange-white fish against a pale pebble floor. The room colors are this author's example set dressing. Their strong graphic contrast is there to make the refraction easy to see, so they are not a fixed palette. What defines the style is: a neutral-to-graphic backdrop with enough pattern or contrast for glass distortion to read, a tinted transparent medium that stays distinct from the backdrop, and small high-chroma subjects inside it. The dominant colors measured from these frames (warm greys and tans, near-black) come from the wood, the top-down floor views and the dark capture border. They are not a background recipe.

contrast_checks.limitation: Two-color checks only. Not a guarantee of complete accessibility or readability over images, textures, glass, video, outlines or animated lighting. Recheck every actual foreground/background pairing in representative frames.

palette.composition_guidance: Use one dominant background and a clear foreground hierarchy. Keep accents subordinate except where the style calls for bold geometric fields. Preserve exact anchors; improve balance through area, spacing and placement rather than hue substitution. Gradient samples and material lighting are not extra base-color licenses.
palette.agent_instruction: Resolve colors in this order: task-provided exact palette, established brand or approved source palette, existing semantic color mappings, then this optional example. Read visual_cues and palette.constraints. Preserve approved anchor values, color families, ink counts and asset colors. Use chroma-js for validation, equivalent normalization and contrast assessment; evaluate gradients only when enabled and appropriate. Select readable token pairs from contrast_checks, otherwise move text onto an existing contrasting backing. Record the resolved tokens and inspect actual composited frames before rendering.

audio_direction.prompt: Based on the topic, audience, objective, narrative, and the visual and motion characteristics of Liquid Glass, suggest an appropriate audio direction. Consider background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or intentional silence. Explain which choices support this particular video; do not assign a fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer to the style.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. When inputs are absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions; do not silently default to instrumental music or invent available audio assets.
audio_direction.integration_guidance: Select or create authorized audio assets separately from visual construction and motion design. Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

suggested_combinations.selection_guidance: Liquid Glass alone is best for hero optical moments where refraction is the feature. Use a hybrid when motion choreography or product pacing needs more structure, keeping true refraction and avoiding plain blur.

supporting_styles.role: Droplet merge and split choreography that drives the glass deformation

suggestions.rationale: Metaball motion supplies continuous organic shape changes, and Liquid Glass supplies the optical treatment, so the refraction must follow the deformation.
suggestions.best_for: Abstract brand loops and fluid UI concept films.
suggestions.video_application: Animate SDF blobs that drive a Three.js transmission mesh or a labeled screen-space displacement over a recognizable #EDEBE3 background with #91ACB0 edge accents.
suggestions.html_application: Render a WebGL hero where pointer or keyboard focus nudges the droplets deterministically, with a static image fallback and the content in the DOM.
consistency_rules: Refraction offsets are derived from the same surface as the shape.
Text never sits behind a refracting region.
avoid: Frosted blur passed off as liquid glass
Chaotic splashing without a baked simulation

supporting_styles.role: Product pacing, framing, and restrained typography

suggestions.rationale: Minimal product motion keeps the optical effect purposeful by framing a single lens or panel around a product feature.
suggestions.best_for: Device and feature launches that emphasize clarity or optics.
suggestions.video_application: Hold slow camera moves on a glass lens passing over product UI, then reveal short titles in #293C49.
suggestions.html_application: Use a feature section where a glass lens magnifies UI details on scroll, with lens size responsive and a reduced-motion static crop.
consistency_rules: Typography stays outside the refracting area.

productionPolicy.principle: Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique.
productionPolicy.style_renderer: Owns visual construction: drawing, geometry, materials, lighting, typography, masks, textures, and specialist asset generation. Use the style-specific recommended technologies and implementation guidance.
productionPolicy.motion_engine: Owns trajectories, transforms, easing, transitions, deformation, and simulation. Select engines or algorithms appropriate to the action, with one owner for each animated property.
productionPolicy.render_pipeline: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.
productionPolicy.integration: Visual and motion layers expose deterministic state at composition time, or supply baked assets or frame sequences. The pipeline supplies seekable time and composes their output. Timeline registration and frame hooks are integration adapters, not substitutes for style-specific rendering or motion.
productionPolicy.selection: Choose only needed stack entries. A technology may serve multiple roles, but document its actual responsibility. Optional authoring, interaction, color, and preprocessing tools are not mandatory renderers or motion engines.

motionReferences.name: Scroll-Driven Section Reveal and Card Stacking
motionReferences.description: Scroll reveals successive sections as overlapping cards. An earlier card stays at a defined anchor while the next rises over it; optional scaling or dimming makes the covered card recede. The active card stays readable and the stack eventually releases or exits as a group.
motion_sequence: Establish the first card and its sticky or pinned anchor.
Bring the next card over the anchored card; optionally reduce the covered card's scale or emphasis to communicate depth.
Repeat with a clear active-card hierarchy and readable holds, then release or exit the stack at a defined endpoint.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Schedule section progression on the video timeline. Calculate each card position and stacking state from time rather than intersection-event history. Give active content a reading hold and preserve a clear focal layer.

suggested_libraries.name: GSAP
suggested_libraries.purpose: Create a paused, seekable timeline for progress, transforms, masks, and controlled easing.

suggested_libraries.name: GSAP ScrollTrigger
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optional interactive-web adapter: bind normalized progress to scroll. Do not require live scrolling for video export.

suggested_libraries.name: PixiJS
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optional 2D implementation of Scroll-Driven Section Reveal and Card Stacking using sprites, graphics, masks, or layered containers. Preserve the selected style; use Three.js when true 3D geometry is required.
suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Use a private ticker and disable autoplay with autoStart: false and sharedTicker: false; stop any already-started application. Load assets, derive scene state directly from composition time, and call app.render() explicitly on updates and seeks. Calling ticker.update() alone does not make cumulative simulation seekable.

suggested_libraries.name: Motion
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optional DOM or SVG implementation of Scroll-Driven Section Reveal and Card Stacking using controlled keyframes or sequences. Verify synchronization with the selected video framework before adopting this route.
suggested_libraries.runtime: browser; motion/react for mounted React components
suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Use the JavaScript entry point for HTML compositions. Pause playback and set animation.time in seconds from composition time, then verify that forward, backward, and direct seeks update the visible result. Motion is an optional animation layer, not a drop-in replacement for the HyperFrames GSAP registration contract; keep the registered GSAP timeline as the framework clock and explicitly synchronize Motion. Use motion/react only within mounted React components.

suggested_libraries.name: tldraw
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optionally author diagram, annotation, or card assets for Scroll-Driven Section Reveal and Card Stacking. Export layers or structured scene data; animate them using the video timeline.
suggested_libraries.runtime: mounted React editor in browser; exported assets for video composition
suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Author diagrams and artwork in a mounted React editor, then export SVG or raster assets using editor.getSvgString or editor.toImage. Await export and split layers deliberately when separate animation is required; a flattened image does not preserve editable shapes. Animate those assets in the chosen framework. Verify signatures against the installed SDK; tldraw is not a video renderer or an automatic timeline adapter.

tech.implementation: Use an anchored outer stage with ordered card layers, explicit z-order, and bounded progress windows. Interactive output can use CSS sticky plus scroll-driven animation, or ScrollTrigger pinning with inner animated wrappers. Animate incoming cards over earlier cards; optionally scale or dim covered cards without hiding unread copy. For video, derive card transforms and coverage from composition time, with finite start and release states.

For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. motionReferences.reference_label: Scroll-Driven Section Reveal and Card Stacking

interaction.progress_driver: Map section entry or a bounded scroll range to card positions, masks, opacity, and explicit stacking order.
interaction.exit_behavior: Preserve a coherent stack when scrolling backward; avoid unexpected duplicate cards or hidden essential copy.

motionReferences.audio_direction_prompt: Based on the topic, mood, medium, and existing audio requirements, suggest whether this action benefits from a restrained sound accent, ambience, music synchronization, or silence. Do not attach a mandatory sound to the pattern or compete with narration.
verification: Seek directly to the start, intermediate states, and end, then compare them with sequential playback.
Check legibility, composition, material consistency, clipping, and visual continuity.
For interactive delivery, check the applicable hover, scroll, keyboard, touch, and reduced-motion behavior; video export must remain independent of live input.
Check front-to-back order, occlusion, contrast, and legibility at every section handoff.
Seek forward and backward through stack stages and confirm consistent card ordering.
motionReferences.adaptation_guidance: Sticky or pinned anchoring, successive overlap, and optional recession are documented stacking mechanics. Scale amount, dimming, offsets, count, and final release are topic and style choices, not fixed values. For video, simulate the same visible states with time-driven transforms rather than live sticky layout.

motionReferences.name: Hover-Driven 3D Voice Card Spatial Interaction
motionReferences.description: A voice or audio card responds to hover and pointer position with bounded perspective tilt. Map vertical pointer offset to horizontal-axis rotation and horizontal offset to vertical-axis rotation; optional raised inner layers add depth. The card returns to its resting pose on exit. Voice playback, waveform display, and audio panning are separate optional features, not consequences of the visual tilt.
motion_sequence: Establish the resting audio card, readable content, and explicit playback controls.
On hover and pointer movement, tilt the card within bounded angles and optionally offset inner layers in depth.
On exit, settle the card back to its resting pose. Play audio only through a separately chosen playback interaction.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Keyframe hover progress, any visible cursor, and card transforms. Place authorized audio on the selected framework timeline. Precompute waveform or spectral data from that audio if the visual reacts to it. Do not require a live pointer or AudioContext during export; a silent visual demonstration is valid when appropriate.

suggested_libraries.name: GSAP
suggested_libraries.purpose: Create a paused, seekable timeline for progress, transforms, masks, and controlled easing.

suggested_libraries.name: Three.js
suggested_libraries.purpose: Render genuine 3D forms or shader treatments when a 2D solution is insufficient.

suggested_libraries.name: Web Audio API
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optional interactive audio playback and spatial panning after an appropriate user action. For video, use framework-owned audio tracks and precomputed analysis rather than a live AudioContext.

suggested_libraries.name: Motion
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optional DOM or SVG implementation of Hover-Driven 3D Voice Card Spatial Interaction using controlled keyframes or sequences. Verify synchronization with the selected video framework before adopting this route.
suggested_libraries.runtime: browser; motion/react for mounted React components
suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Use the JavaScript entry point for HTML compositions. Pause playback and set animation.time in seconds from composition time, then verify that forward, backward, and direct seeks update the visible result. Motion is an optional animation layer, not a drop-in replacement for the HyperFrames GSAP registration contract; keep the registered GSAP timeline as the framework clock and explicitly synchronize Motion. Use motion/react only within mounted React components.

tech.implementation: Use CSS perspective with bounded rotateX and rotateY values driven by normalized pointer offsets; use preserve-3d and depth offsets only when inner layers need separation. Motion or GSAP can animate these browser transforms. Keep text legible and separate audio playback controls from tilt. For video, evaluate authored pointer and transform states from composition time and let the video framework own audio; do not depend on live hover or AudioContext playback.
tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

good_fit: Glass, skeuomorphic, Y2K, or restrained 3D interface treatments
adapt_or_omit_when: The topic has no audio content and the voice-card metaphor adds confusion.
Tilt or depth makes speaker labels, captions, or controls unreadable.
Playback is unavailable, unsupported, or presented as working without an actual audio asset.

Consider {{motion_pattern}} for audio content in {{subject}}, using {{visual_style}} and {{render_pipeline}}. In video, keyframe the pointer response and use framework-owned audio. Suggest sound behavior from the topic; visual 3D tilt does not imply automatic playback or spatial panning. For Canvas or WebGL, verify explicit repaint on direct seek as well as sequential playback.

interaction.progress_driver: Normalize pointer position relative to the card bounds and map it to bounded rotateX and rotateY values under perspective. Optional depth lift has its own bounded parameter. Define focus or touch behavior separately.
interaction.exit_behavior: Settle rotations and lift toward the neutral pose. Do not automatically start, stop, or pan audio merely because the card tilts.

motionReferences.audio_direction_prompt: Based on the topic and available content, suggest a voice excerpt, narration, instrumental bed, a restrained interaction accent, or a silent demonstration. Keep voice content intelligible and avoid competing vocals. Spatial panning is optional: explain its purpose and verify the actual output rather than assuming that a tilted card requires spatial audio.
verification: Seek directly to the start, intermediate states, and end, then compare them with sequential playback.
Check legibility, composition, material consistency, clipping, and visual continuity.
For interactive delivery, check the applicable hover, scroll, keyboard, touch, and reduced-motion behavior; video export must remain independent of live input.
Check tilted text, card clipping, controls, rest-state recovery, and any visible cursor timing.
If audio is included, verify actual playback, waveform alignment, intelligible speech, channel behavior, and synchronization.
motionReferences.adaptation_guidance: Pointer-driven perspective tilt and depth-layer separation are documented 3D card mechanics. A voice card combines those mechanics with audio content; it is a composite design, not a single standardized preset. Tilt bounds, spring response, waveform, playback interaction, and any spatial audio are chosen for the topic. Keep visual depth distinct from genuine 3D sound.

motionReferences.name: Scroll-Driven Chaptered Scene Transition
motionReferences.description: Scroll progress coordinates a handoff between narrative chapters. An outgoing scene yields to an incoming scene through a chosen fade, wipe, panel rotation, or shared-element move; text and media states change with the same progress. Clear start and end states preserve reading order in both scroll directions.
motion_sequence: Establish the outgoing chapter and a readable closing state.
Across a defined progress window, coordinate outgoing and incoming scene states with one selected transition treatment and synchronized copy.
Resolve the incoming chapter into its readable state before beginning the next handoff; reversing progress retraces the same transition.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Schedule chapter windows and transition intervals on composition time. Explicitly choose the handoff type. If the style requires a continuous shot, use a coherent camera or spatial handoff instead of an incompatible cut.

motionReferences.name: Swipe Card Carousel
motionReferences.description: Move a row or track of cards horizontally so one item or a small group is active and readable. Swipe, button, or keyboard navigation can drive an interactive version. Unlike vertical card stacking, the primary structure is a horizontal sequence with clear item selection.
motion_sequence: Establish the active card, neighboring context, and navigation affordances.
Advance the track in a clear direction and settle the next card into the reading position.
Hold the active card, then continue or end with a deliberate selection state.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Keyframe selected card indices and track offsets with planned reading holds. If demonstrating swipe, author a visible gesture or pointer. Avoid relying on drag velocity, user input, or autoplay state for the exported video.

suggested_libraries.name: PhotoSwipe
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optional image-gallery dialog with swipe navigation, zoom, pan and thumbnail opening or closing transitions for interactive web delivery.
suggested_libraries.runtime: browser; initialize only after the gallery DOM is mounted
suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Use for interactive image viewing only when the task includes a web gallery or lightbox. Define accurate intrinsic image dimensions and responsive sources. Retain direct image links as a fallback, meaningful image alternatives, usable keyboard navigation, focus return and reduced-motion behavior. Initialize after mounting and destroy on cleanup; access the core instance only after opening. Preserve original image colors and established palette tokens when styling controls. PhotoSwipe owns its dialog gestures and transitions; do not attach another animation owner to those properties. Captions require a deliberate custom UI or suitable plugin rather than assuming a built-in caption feature.
suggested_libraries.import_guidance: Use PhotoSwipeLightbox from 'photoswipe/lightbox', load 'photoswipe/style.css', and set pswpModule to () => import('photoswipe'). Check exports and API signatures against the installed version.

For rendered video, recreate the chosen thumbnail expansion, swipe, zoom, pan and reading holds as authored DOM/SVG/Canvas transforms driven by GSAP and the selected framework clock. Do not depend on live touch input, dynamic dialog state or asynchronous lightbox transitions for exported frames. Preserve HyperFrames as primary and Remotion as the existing conditional fallback.
suggested_libraries.selection_guidance: Designed primarily as an image lightbox dialog, not a general inline carousel. Use native scroll snapping or a suitable carousel library for inline cards, mixed interactive card content or persistent neighboring cards. PhotoSwipe does not generate the artwork or determine its visual style.

This does not replace the existing inline horizontal card track, snap-selection motion or its video adaptation. Choose a suitable carousel implementation when neighboring cards, inline layout or rich card interactions are required.

Card styling, spacing, motion response, and reading holds are design choices. A carousel can have finite endpoints or a deliberately configured loop; neither infinite autoplay nor a particular spring is inherent to the motion. Video uses an authored track path instead of a live drag engine.

motionReferences.name: Fluid Morphing Energy Orb
motionReferences.description: Animate a cohesive orb through controlled fluid-like deformation, surface flow, and optional emission. The supplied blue appearance is a palette example, not a fixed requirement. This is a bounded form treatment, distinct from pointer-driven light trails and general fluid simulation.
motion_sequence: Establish a readable orb silhouette, surface treatment, and stable visual center.
Develop restrained pulses, folds, lobes, or surface flow while retaining the dominant orb form.
Settle, transform into a purposeful final shape, or close a designed loop with coherent silhouette and lighting.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Compute deformation from time, seeded procedural fields, or baked geometry. Optional audio reactivity must use verified precomputed analysis. Keep the shape and emission bounded and preserve the final form; do not claim physically accurate fluid behavior without a suitable simulation.

Add bloom only when the material fits the style; validated fluid collisions require a separate simulation workflow.

motionReferences.name: Scroll-Driven Storytelling
motionReferences.description: Coordinate a complete narrative through a series of progress-driven states, aligning copy, imagery, diagrams, and camera framing with the story. This is an orchestration pattern: it may reference compatible chapter transitions, pinned heroes, or card reveals but does not require all of them.
motion_sequence: Define the question or premise and introduce the story's focal subject.
Advance through purposeful stages that reveal context, mechanism, comparison, or consequence.
Resolve the story into a conclusion with enough reading time and a coherent final state.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Turn the progress journey into a timed storyboard with explicit scene windows and reading holds. Use a master progress parameter or finite scene-local parameters evaluated from time. A video tells the same story without requiring the viewer to scroll.

suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Use a private ticker and disable autoplay with autoStart: false and sharedTicker: false; stop any already-started application. Load assets, derive scene state directly from composition time, and call app.render() explicitly on updates and seeks. Calling ticker.update() alone does not make cumulative simulation seekable.

suggested_libraries.name: Motion
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optional DOM or SVG implementation of Scroll-Driven Storytelling using controlled keyframes or sequences. Verify synchronization with the selected video framework before adopting this route.
suggested_libraries.runtime: browser; motion/react for mounted React components
suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Use the JavaScript entry point for HTML compositions. Pause playback and set animation.time in seconds from composition time, then verify that forward, backward, and direct seeks update the visible result. Motion is an optional animation layer, not a drop-in replacement for the HyperFrames GSAP registration contract; keep the registered GSAP timeline as the framework clock and explicitly synchronize Motion. Use motion/react only within mounted React components.

suggested_libraries.name: tldraw
suggested_libraries.purpose: Optionally author diagram, annotation, or card assets for Scroll-Driven Storytelling. Export layers or structured scene data; animate them using the video timeline.
suggested_libraries.runtime: mounted React editor in browser; exported assets for video composition
suggested_libraries.integration_guidance: Author diagrams and artwork in a mounted React editor, then export SVG or raster assets using editor.getSvgString or editor.toImage. Await export and split layers deliberately when separate animation is required; a flattened image does not preserve editable shapes. Animate those assets in the chosen framework. Verify signatures against the installed SDK; tldraw is not a video renderer or an automatic timeline adapter.

tech.implementation: Define meaningful story steps, the visual state for each step, and optional continuous progress inside a step. Interactive delivery can use ScrollTrigger timelines or an existing step/progress observer such as Scrollama, with CSS sticky when a graphic should remain visible. Keep copy and graphics synchronized through the same story state. For video, schedule steps and within-step progress on the framework timeline with reading holds; evaluate the full visible state directly on each seek.
tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

good_fit: Illustrated or cinematic sequences with a coherent beginning, development, and conclusion
adapt_or_omit_when: There is no meaningful narrative progression to organize.
Scroll-driven spectacle replaces an explanation or hides essential copy.
Nested patterns produce conflicting progress drivers, projection, material rules, or unreadable motion.

motionReferences.executable_prompt_template:
Consider {{motion_pattern}} to organize {{subject}} in {{visual_style}} with {{render_pipeline}}. Through {{motion_parameters}}, define a premise, meaningful story steps, corresponding copy and visual states, optional within-step progress, and a conclusion. Let scroll select or advance these states in interactive delivery; schedule the same journey with reading holds for video. Use sticky graphics, camera movement, or other catalog motions only when they serve the topic. Preserve reading order and state coherence on backward and direct seeks rather than combining unrelated effects. Resolve library choices from this pattern's tech guidance and library_options, and follow render_contract for the selected framework. Choose parameters from the topic and style. For Canvas or WebGL, verify explicit repaint on direct seek as well as sequential playback.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.

interaction.progress_driver: Map a finite scroll journey to ordered narrative states and optional chapter-local progress. Provide accessible reading order and usable static or reduced-motion states.
interaction.exit_behavior: Backward scrolling returns to the matching narrative state without contradictory copy or duplicated content.

motionReferences.audio_direction_prompt: Based on the topic, mood, medium, and existing audio requirements, suggest whether this action benefits from a restrained sound accent, ambience, music synchronization, or silence. Do not attach a mandatory sound to the pattern or compete with narration.
verification: Seek directly to the start, intermediate states, and end, then compare them with sequential playback.
Check legibility, composition, material consistency, clipping, and visual continuity.
For interactive delivery, check the applicable hover, scroll, keyboard, touch, and reduced-motion behavior; video export must remain independent of live input.
Check that each stage contributes a clear idea and that copy matches the visible state.
Verify direct seeking at stage boundaries and optional nested-pattern handoffs without conflicting time drivers.
motionReferences.adaptation_guidance: Step-based visual updates and optional within-step progress are documented scrollytelling mechanics. Narration structure, camera motion, media choice, sticky framing, and pacing depend on the topic. A whole story coordinates multiple meaningful states; it is broader than one chapter transition and does not require all catalog effects.

motionReferences.name: Cursor-Driven Camera Orbit
motionReferences.description: Establish a central 3D subject, a fixed orbit target and a bounded resting viewpoint. Map normalized pointer position to limited camera azimuth and elevation while retaining target and orbit radius. Smoothly return to the resting view on exit; provide keyboard or touch controls and a static reduced-motion view.

motionReferences.name: Punctuation Zoom
motionReferences.description: Use actual punctuation as a persistent shared element. Move the view toward it, enlarge it until it occludes the scene and reveal the next composition underneath. Do not substitute an unrelated rectangle or generic fade.
motion_sequence: Establish a readable sentence with an actual punctuation mark as its final visible shared element.
Move the view toward the mark and enlarge it continuously until it occludes the frame.
Reveal the next scene inside the same punctuation field and hold a clear incoming composition.
